items.summary: Background Transcutaneous auricular vagus nerve stimulation (taVNS) has shown promise for enhancing cognition and emotion regulation. Moreover, the underlying mechanisms of taVNS are still not well understood. items.title: REALITY AS A QUANTUM MIST OF NODES OF OSCILLATING FIELDS THROUGH INTERACTION Toward a Copernican Revolution in the Ontology of Science
items.summary: Abstract This White Paper proposes a Copernican revolution in the ontology of science. The central thesis is that reality is not composed of discrete entities located in a neutral spatiotemporal container, but is a quantum mist of nodes of oscillating fields through interaction. items.title: Infection-related research in Parkinson’s disease: an exploratory trends analysis
items.summary: Background Infection and Parkinson's disease (PD) appear to interact through complex mechanisms. Infection may promote the occurrence and progression of pathological processes related to PD, while PD and its associated dysfunctions may increase the risk of infection. This study depicts the evolution, thematic structure, and emerging directions of infection-related research in PD. Methods Publications related to infection and PD from 1999 to June 30, 2026 were retrieved from the WoSCC and Scopus databases. items.title: Prognostic prediction model construction and validation based on regional cerebral oxygen saturation and bispectral index monitoring in pediatric traumatic brain injury
items.summary: Background Continuous multimodal cerebral monitoring may improve detection and management of secondary injury after pediatric moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury (msTBI). We developed and validated a prognostic model for 6-month functional outcome integrating regional cerebral oxygen saturation (rScO₂), bispectral index (BIS), clinical and biomarker data. Methods Prospective cohort of 93 children with msTBI monitored with rScO₂ and BIS (monitoring group) and a retrospective control cohort of 66 children without such monitoring. Primary outcome was Glasgow Outcome Scale (GOS) at 6 months.

items.title: From Mechanistic Models to AI Synergy: A Roadmap for Predictive and Personalized Biology
items.summary: Two paradigms now drive the life sciences. One is the explanatory depth of mathematical modeling, the other the predictive power of artificial intelligence. For decades, mechanistic models have offered a rigorous, hypothesis-driven framework for dissecting biological processes, while AI has proven itself at finding patterns in the large, high-dimensional datasets of modern biology. Each has delivered major advances on its own. Together they promise a synthesis that could redefine the boundaries of biological inquiry. items.title: Prevalence and factors associated with suicidal ideation and suicidal behavior among police personnel in Kerala, India: a cross-sectional study
items.summary: Introduction Although police personnel are exposed to substantial occupational stress and Kerala has one of the highest suicide rates in India, evidence on suicidal ideation and suicidal behavior among police personnel in the state remains limited. This study estimated the prevalence of suicidal ideation and suicidal behavior and identified their associated factors among police personnel in Kerala, India. items.title: FieldTrip: Open Source Software for Advanced Analysis of MEG, EEG, and Invasive Electrophysiological Data
items.summary: This paper describes FieldTrip, an open source software package that we developed for the analysis of MEG, EEG, and other electrophysiological data. The software is implemented as a MATLAB toolbox and includes a complete set of consistent and user-friendly high-level functions that allow experimental neuroscientists to analyze experimental data. It includes algorithms for simple and advanced analysis, such as time-frequency analysis using multitapers, source reconstruction using dipoles, distributed sources and beamformers, connectivity analysis, and nonparametric statistical permutation tests

items.title: Social Relationships and Mortality Risk: A Meta-analytic Review
items.summary: BACKGROUND: The quality and quantity of individuals' social relationships has been linked not only to mental health but also to both morbidity and mortality. OBJECTIVES: This meta-analytic review was conducted to determine the extent to which social relationships influence risk for mortality, which aspects of social relationships are most highly predictive, and which factors may moderate the risk. items.summary: Wayne Rasband of NIH has created ImageJ, an open source Java-written program that is now at version 1.31 and is used for many imaging applications, including those that that span the gamut from skin analysis to neuroscience. items.summary: Background Herpes simplex encephalitis (HSE) survivors frequently experience neuropsychiatric sequelae, including depressive symptoms, but the biological correlates underlying post-HSE depression remain incompletely understood. items.title: WGCNA: an R package for weighted correlation network analysis
items.summary: BACKGROUND: Correlation networks are increasingly being used in bioinformatics applications. For example, weighted gene co-expression network analysis is a systems biology method for describing the correlation patterns among genes across microarray samples.
